rationales: Forestry is an established field concerned with forests and their management.
Farming is an established practice of cultivating crops and raising animals.
Biotechnology is a relatively recent profession that applies biological processes and organisms to practical uses.
Horticulture is an established field concerned with growing garden plants and crops.
A theory is a well-supported explanation, not the recorded observations themselves.
Bioinformatics uses computational methods to analyze biological information.
Data are facts and values collected through observations and experiments.
A law describes a consistent natural relationship, rather than a collection of observations.
Some fungi are multicellular, but they are not the expected example of a simple multicellular organism here.
Algae such as Spirogyra are simple multicellular organisms.
Bacteria are unicellular organisms.
Plants are generally complex multicellular organisms.
Lipids are not the other major component of ribosomes.
Ribosomes contain roughly equal amounts of rRNA and protein.
DNA is not a major structural component of ribosomes.
Starch is not a component of ribosomes.
Filtration is the separation of substances through a filter, not cytoplasm shrinkage.
Endocytosis is the uptake of material into a cell.
Turgor pressure is the pressure of cell contents against the cell wall.
Plasmolysis is the shrinkage of cytoplasm away from the cell wall, usually due to water loss.
Glycolysis is the first stage of cellular respiration.
The Krebs cycle follows glycolysis and precedes the final stage.
The electron transport chain is the final stage of aerobic cellular respiration.
Fermentation is an alternative anaerobic pathway, not the final stage of aerobic respiration.
Entomology is the study of insects.
Taxonomy is the science of naming and classifying organisms.
Palaeontology is the study of fossils and ancient life.
Pharmacology is the study of drugs and their effects.
Flaccid describes a limp cell, not specifically cytoplasm shrinking away from the cell wall.
Plasmolysis is the shrinkage of cytoplasm away from the cell wall.
Plasmodesmata are channels connecting neighboring plant cells.
Turgor is the pressure of cell contents against the cell wall.
A community consists of populations of different species living together.
A habitat is the area or environment where an organism lives.
A population is a group of the same species living in an area.
The ecosphere is the global zone of Earth where life exists.
Deductions are conclusions drawn from a hypothesis or observations, not the basic initial step.
Observations are the basic starting point of the biological method.
A hypothesis is a proposed explanation formed after observations.
Experimentation tests a hypothesis and comes after earlier steps.
Carolus Linnaeus introduced the binomial system of naming organisms.
Ernst Haeckel was a biologist but did not introduce binomial nomenclature.
Robert Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification system.
Aristotle made early contributions to biology but did not introduce binomial nomenclature.
Epidermal tissue is a plant tissue, not a type of connective tissue.
Support tissues is a broad description and is not the specific connective-tissue option sought here.
Adipose tissue is a connective tissue that stores fat.
Ground tissue is a type of plant tissue.
Six months is longer than the typical red blood cell lifespan.
Two months is shorter than the typical red blood cell lifespan.
Seven months is longer than the typical red blood cell lifespan.
A red blood cell typically lives about 120 days, or roughly four months.
Prophase is only one stage of cell division and does not occupy most of the cell cycle.
Interphase typically accounts for at least 90% of the cell cycle.
Anaphase is a brief stage of cell division.
Telophase is a brief stage of cell division.
Amylase breaks down starch, not protein stains.
Lipase breaks down fats, not protein stains.
Protease breaks down proteins and is used to remove protein stains.
Thiamine is a vitamin, not an enzyme for removing stains.
